preview_en:
After suffering their first defeat of the La Liga season, Deportivo A Coruña look to bounce back when they host an in-form Real Betis in what is a first H2H since 2018.

Match News and Current Form

Deportivo A Coruña and the free-scoring Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang were finally stopped on Wednesday, as Sevilla ran out 1-0 winners at the Riazor. The newly-promoted hosts start this round in the top seven regardless thanks to a five-game unbeaten start (W2, D3), but that may be difficult to maintain with three games against sides who qualified for Europe last season in their next four fixtures. Antonio Hidalgo’s side will look to lean on their home form to ensure their top-flight return is a successful one, as that defeat to Sevilla was just their second from their last ten games at the Riazor (W6, D2).

Real Betis have made a flying start to their campaign, winning six of their seven games in all competitions, including each of the last four. A 1-0 victory over Getafe on Thursday lifted Manuel Pellegrini’s men into the top three, with this just the second time they’ve picked up as many as 15 points from their first six La Liga fixtures this century. Los Verdiblancos are now targeting five successive competitive wins for the first time since November 2023, and should be confident given that they’ve lost just twice on their travels since the start of April (W4, D3).

Head-to-Head History

Betis have lost just one of the last nine top-flight H2Hs (W3, D5), though Deportivo have lost only one of their last eight La Liga trips to Betis (W4, D3).

Hot Stats and Streaks

Deportivo haven't kept a clean sheet in any of their last seven competitive games.

Deportivo have had fewer shots than their opponents in all six of their matches so far this season.

Betis’ last eight competitive victories have all come by a single-goal margin.

Nine of Betis’ last ten away matches across all competitions have seen both teams score.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Both of Luismi Cruz ’s goal contributions this season (G1, A1) have come before half-time, and he’s unbeaten when scoring at club level since February 2023 (W9, D4). Betis centre-back Marc Bartra has scored three times across all competitions this term, with each of his last four strikes now coming on the road.

Angeliño is suspended for Deportivo, while Betis appear to have no new injury worries.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

With their current streak of narrow victories, backing Betis to win by a single-goal margin looks like a solid option.

Author: Tom Penn
